greek: Καὶ εἶπεν κύριος τῷ Αβραμ Ἔξελθε ἐκ τῆς γῆς σου καὶ ἐκ τῆς συγγενείας σου καὶ ἐκ τοῦ οἴκου τοῦ πατρός σου εἰς τὴν γῆν, ἣν ἄν σοι δείξω·
hint: The Lord calls Abram out of his land and his father's house.

notes.text: The Hebrew *lek-lĕkā*, *go for yourself*. The Greek has ἐξέρχομαι, *go out of*, the verb of Acts 7:3, where Stephen quotes the verse: Ἔξελθε ἐκ τῆς γῆς σου καὶ ἐκ τῆς συγγενείας σου.
συγγένεια, first *sameness of descent*, then *kin*; the Hebrew *môladtĕkā*, *your birthplace, your kindred*.
Glossed again, first in this chapter.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: And [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] to [[name:Αβραμ]] [[go out of|go out of, come out, go away and march off, go forth|ἐξέρχομαι]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of the earth|of the earth, of the land, of the ground|γῆ]] of you and [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of the sameness of descent|of the sameness of descent, of the family and relationship and kin, of the ties of kindred and family connexion and influence, of the kinsfolk and kinsmen, of the families|συγγένεια]] of you and [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of the house|of the house, of the abode and dwelling, of the room and chamber, of the house of a god and temple, of the household goods and substance, of the household and family|οἶκος]] [[of the father|of the father, of the grandfather|πατήρ]] of you [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[the earth|the earth, the land, the ground|γῆ]], which ever to you [[I may bring to light|I may bring to light, I may display and exhibit, I may set before one, I may show and point out, I may tell and explain and teach, I may show and prove, I may inform against, I may offer and proffer, I may cause, I may welcome and greet and pledge|δείκνυμι]];

names.gloss: (Αβραμ, from Hebrew ʾAbrām, "the father is exalted")

greek: καὶ ποιήσω σε εἰς ἔθνος μέγα καὶ εὐλογήσω σε καὶ μεγαλυνῶ τὸ ὄνομά σου, καὶ ἔσῃ εὐλογητός·
hint: A great nation, a great name, and Abram blessed.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wehyēh bĕrākâ*, *and be a blessing*. The Greek has *and you will be blessed*, εὐλογητός, one sense, plain text.
μεγαλύνω, *to make great*, the verb of Mary's song, Luke 1:46.

reading: and [[I will make|I will make, I will do, I will produce, I will create|ποιέω]] you [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[a number of people accustomed to live together|a number of people accustomed to live together, a company and body of men, a host, swarms and flocks, a nation and people, the nations and gentiles, a special class, a caste and tribe, a sex|ἔθνος]] [[big|big, great, tall, full-grown, vast and high, spacious and wide, strong and mighty, violent, loud, prevailing, weighty and important|μέγας]] and [[I will speak well of|I will speak well of, I will praise, I will honour, I will bless|εὐλογέω]] you and [[I will make great|I will make great and powerful, I will exalt and strengthen, I will make great by word and extol and magnify, I will aggravate|μεγαλύνω]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] of you, and you will be blessed;

greek: καὶ εὐλογήσω τοὺς εὐλογοῦντάς σε, καὶ τοὺς καταρωμένους σε καταράσομαι· καὶ ἐνευλογηθήσονται ἐν σοὶ πᾶσαι αἱ φυλαὶ τῆς γῆς.
hint: All the tribes of the earth will be blessed in Abram.

notes.lemma: ἐνευλογηθήσονται ἐν σοὶ πᾶσαι αἱ φυλαὶ τῆς γῆς
notes.text: Paul quotes it at Galatians 3:8, Ἐνευλογηθήσονται ἐν σοὶ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, with *all the nations* from 18:18. Middle Liddell gives ἐνευλογέομαι one sense, *to be blessed in* one, so it is plain text, and the Greek's own ἐν σοί follows it: *will be blessed in in you*.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is singular, *ûmĕqallelkā*, *the one who makes light of you*, and uses another verb from *ʾāʾōr*, *I will curse*. The Greek has the plural and καταράομαι for both.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads εὐλογηθήσονται, without ἐν; the Berlin papyrus, 911, has it.

reading: and [[I will speak well of|I will speak well of, I will praise, I will honour, I will bless|εὐλογέω]] [[the ones speaking well of|the ones speaking well of, praising, honouring, blessing|εὐλογέω]] you, and [[the ones calling down curses upon|the ones calling down curses upon, imprecating upon, cursing and execrating, uttering imprecations|καταράομαι]] you [[I will call down curses upon|I will call down curses upon, I will imprecate upon, I will curse and execrate, I will utter imprecations|καταράομαι]]; and will be blessed in in you [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[the races|the races, the tribes, the bodies united by ties of blood and descent, the clans, the tribes by local habitation, the hundreds and counties, the contingents furnished by a tribe, the brigades|φυλή]] [[of the earth|of the earth, of the land, of the ground|γῆ]].

greek: καὶ ἐπορεύθη Αβραμ, καθάπερ ἐλάλησεν αὐτῷ κύριος, καὶ ᾤχετο μετʼ αὐτοῦ Λωτ· Αβραμ δὲ ἦν ἐτῶν ἑβδομήκοντα πέντε, ὅτε ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ Χαρραν.
hint: Abram goes, and Lot with him, at seventy-five.

notes.text: Filed inside καθά, *according as, just as*, the chain of 7:9.
οἴχομαι, *to be gone, have gone*: Middle Liddell gives its imperfect the sense of a pluperfect, *had gone*.
λαλέω is first *to talk, chat, prattle*; *to speak*, like λέγω, is its New Testament use, third in the entry.

names.gloss: (Λωτ, from Hebrew Lôṭ, of uncertain meaning)
(Χαρραν, from Hebrew Ḥārān, the city Harran)

greek: καὶ ἔλαβεν Αβραμ τὴν Σαραν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸν Λωτ υἱὸν τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ καὶ πάντα τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτῶν, ὅσα ἐκτήσαντο, καὶ πᾶσαν ψυχήν, ἣν ἐκτήσαντο ἐν Χαρραν, καὶ ἐξήλθοσαν πορευθῆναι εἰς γῆν Χανααν καὶ ἦλθον εἰς γῆν Χανααν. —
hint: Abram takes Sarai, Lot and all they had into the land of Canaan.

notes.text: ὑπάρχω's participle used as a noun, so the entry's first sense for it: *existing circumstances, present advantages*, then *one's possessions*. The Hebrew *rĕkûšām*, *their goods*.
The Hebrew *hannepeš ʾăšer-ʿāśû*, *the souls that they had made*: the people acquired in Haran. The Greek has κτάομαι, *procured for themselves*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads Σαρα, and ἐκ Χαρραν; the Berlin papyrus, 911, has Σαραν, and Coislinianus, M, ἐν.
Rahlfs prints a dash after the verse, closing a section.

names.gloss: (Σαρα, from Hebrew Śāray, usually connected with śārâ, "princess")
(Χανααν, from Hebrew Kĕnaʿan, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ διώδευσεν Αβραμ τὴν γῆν εἰς τὸ μῆκος αὐτῆς ἕως τοῦ τόπου Συχεμ ἐπὶ τὴν δρῦν τὴν ὑψηλήν· οἱ δὲ Χαναναῖοι τότε κατῴκουν τὴν γῆν.
hint: Abram passes through the land to the high oak at Shechem.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʿad ʾēlôn môreh*, *as far as the oak of Moreh*, a name, usually connected with *yārâ*, *to teach*. The Greek has *the high oak*.
[[flag]] Not in the Hebrew: *through the land, into its length*.
διοδεύω, *to travel through*, one sense, plain text.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus leaves out the first τὴν γῆν.

greek: καὶ ὤφθη κύριος τῷ Αβραμ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Τῷ σπέρματί σου δώσω τὴν γῆν ταύτην. καὶ ᾠκοδόμησεν ἐκεῖ Αβραμ θυσιαστήριον κυρίῳ τῷ ὀφθέντι αὐτῷ.
hint: The Lord appears and promises the land to Abram's seed; Abram builds an altar.

notes.lemma: Τῷ σπέρματί σου δώσω τὴν γῆν ταύτην
notes.text: Stephen gives the promise at Acts 7:5, δοῦναι αὐτῷ εἰς κατάσχεσιν αὐτὴν καὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ, and Paul reads τῷ σπέρματί σου as singular at Galatians 3:16.
The aorist passive of ὁράω, *was seen*: the verb of the appearances in 1 Corinthians 15:5–8.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: καὶ ἀπέστη ἐκεῖθεν εἰς τὸ ὄρος κατʼ ἀνατολὰς Βαιθηλ καὶ ἔστησεν ἐκεῖ τὴν σκηνὴν αὐτοῦ, Βαιθηλ κατὰ θάλασσαν καὶ Αγγαι κατʼ ἀνατολάς· καὶ ᾠκοδόμησεν ἐκεῖ θυσιαστήριον τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ ἐπεκαλέσατο ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι κυρίου.
hint: Between Bethel and Ai Abram pitches his tent and calls on the name of the Lord.

notes.lemma: Βαιθηλ κατὰ θάλασσαν καὶ Αγγαι κατʼ ἀνατολάς
notes.text: *Bethel toward the sea and Ai toward the risings*: the Hebrew *miyyām* and *miqqedem*, west and east, named from the sea and the sunrise, as the Greek keeps them.
The second aorist of ἀφίστημι, intransitive: the entry's sense B, *to stand away*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads ἐν before the second Βαιθηλ; Coislinianus, M, does not.

greek: καὶ ἀπῆρεν Αβραμ καὶ πορευθεὶς ἐστρατοπέδευσεν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ.
hint: Abram sets out and encamps in the desert.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *hālôk wĕnāsôaʿ hannegbâ*, *going on and journeying toward the Negeb*, the south. The Greek has *encamped in the desert*.
ἐρῆμος is an adjective, *desolate, lone*; used as a noun, ἡ ἐρῆμος (sc. χώρα), its first tagged noun sense is *desert parts*.

greek: Καὶ ἐγένετο λιμὸς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ κατέβη Αβραμ εἰς Αἴγυπτον παροικῆσαι ἐκεῖ, ὅτι ἐνίσχυσεν ὁ λιμὸς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
hint: Famine drives Abram down into Egypt.

notes.text: παροικέω, *to dwell beside*, and in the New Testament *to sojourn*: the word of Hebrews 11:9, πίστει παρῴκησεν εἰς γῆν τῆς ἐπαγγελίας.
Not in Middle Liddell; LSJ gives ἐνισχύω *strengthen, confirm*, and intransitive *prevail*.

hint: The Egyptians see that the woman is very beautiful.

reading: [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[at which time|at which time, when, since, whenever|ἡνίκα]] [[went in|went in, went into and entered, came into, came in, came upon|εἰσέρχομαι]] [[name:Αβραμ]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[name:Αἴγυπτον]], [[having seen|having seen, having perceived, having beheld, having looked at|ὁράω]] [[name:Αἰγύπτιοι]] [[the woman|the woman, the mistress and lady, the wife and spouse|γυνή]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[beautiful|beautiful, beauteous, fair, good|καλός]] was, and kept on being, [[very|very, very much, exceedingly, violently, far, most certainly|σφόδρα]],

greek: καὶ εἶδον αὐτὴν οἱ ἄρχοντες Φαραω καὶ ἐπῄνεσαν αὐτὴν πρὸς Φαραω καὶ εἰσήγαγον αὐτὴν εἰς τὸν οἶκον Φαραω·
hint: Pharaoh's rulers praise her, and she is taken into his house.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is passive, *wattuqqaḥ hāʾiššâ*, *and the woman was taken*. The Greek has the rulers *lead her in*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads πρός for εἰς.

reading: and [[saw|saw, perceived, beheld, looked at|ὁράω]] her [[the rulers|the rulers, the commanders, the chiefs, the captains, the chief magistrates|ἄρχων]] of [[name:Φαραω]] and [[approved|approved, applauded, commended, complimented publicly and panegyrized, recommended and exhorted and advised, thanked, declined|ἐπαινέω]] her [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Φαραω]] and [[led in|led in, led into and introduced, admitted, imported, called in, brought in and brought forward|εἰσάγω]] her [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[the house|the house, the abode and dwelling, the room and chamber, the house of a god and temple, the household goods and substance, the household and family|οἶκος]] of [[name:Φαραω]];

names.gloss: (Φαραω, from Hebrew Parʿōh, from the Egyptian for "great house")

greek: καὶ τῷ Αβραμ εὖ ἐχρήσαντο διʼ αὐτήν, καὶ ἐγένοντο αὐτῷ πρόβατα καὶ μόσχοι καὶ ὄνοι, παῖδες καὶ παιδίσκαι, ἡμίονοι καὶ κάμηλοι.
hint: Abram is treated well and given flocks, servants, mules and camels.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew has *waʾătōnōt*, *and she-asses*. The Greek has *mules*, ἡμίονοι, *half-asses*.
χράομαι is first *to use*; Perseus tags *consulting* and *using an oracle* ahead of it, which describe where the sense comes from and are left out. With εὖ, *treated well*.
μόσχος has two entries; the second is the animal, *a calf*, the first *a young shoot*.

reading: and to [[name:Αβραμ]] [[well|well, luckily, happily, well off|εὖ]] [[used|used, had and used, indulged, experienced and suffered and were subject to, came to, lived under, made use of, treated, were intimate with, were in need and yearned after, had in use and possessed|χράομαι]] [[through|through, throughout and over, during, by aid of and by means of, by reason of, because of, for the sake of|διά + accusative]] her, and [[came into being|came to be, arose, were brought into existence|γίνομαι]] to him [[things that walk forward|things that walk forward, cattle, flocks and herds, horses, small cattle, sheep|πρόβατον]] and [[calves|calves, young bulls, heifers and young cows, boys and girls and maids, young animals|μόσχος]] and [[asses|asses, beasts of burden, windlasses and pulleys, upper millstones, beakers and wine-cups|ὄνος]], [[children|children, sons, daughters, grandchildren, boys and youths and lads, girls and maidens, slaves and servants and men and maids|παῖς]] and [[young girls|young girls, maidens, young slaves, courtesans|παιδίσκη]], [[half-asses|half-asses, mules, wild asses|ἡμίονος]] and [[camels|camels, the camels in an army, the camelry and camel-brigade|κάμηλος]].

greek: καὶ ἤτασεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν Φαραω ἐτασμοῖς μεγάλοις καὶ πονηροῖς καὶ τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ περὶ Σαρας τῆς γυναικὸς Αβραμ.
hint: God afflicts Pharaoh and his house because of Sarai.

notes.lemma: ὁ θεὸς … ἐτασμοῖς μεγάλοις καὶ πονηροῖς
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayĕnaggaʿ YHWH … nĕgāʿîm gĕdōlîm*, *YHWH struck … with great strokes*. The Greek has ὁ θεός, and adds *and toilsome*.
ἐτάζω, *to examine, test*, with its noun: *examined … with trials*. ἐτασμός is not in Middle Liddell; LSJ gives it the sense of ἔτασις, *trial, affliction*.

reading: and [[examined|examined, tested|ἐτάζω]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[name:Φαραω]] [[to trials|to trials, to afflictions|ἐτασμός]] [[with big|with big, with great, with tall, with full-grown, with vast and high, with spacious and wide, with strong and mighty, with violent, with loud, with prevailing, with weighty and important|μέγας]] and [[with toilsome|with toilsome, with painful, with grievous, with good-for-nothing, with bad and worthless, with wicked|πονηρός]] and [[the house|the house, the abode and dwelling, the room and chamber, the house of a god and temple, the household goods and substance, the household and family|οἶκος]] of him [[round about|round about, around, about and near, about and for and on account of, about and concerning, for very|περί + genitive]] of [[name:Σαρας]] [[of the woman|of the woman, of the mistress and lady, of the wife and spouse|γυνή]] of [[name:Αβραμ]].

greek: καλέσας δὲ Φαραω τὸν Αβραμ εἶπεν Τί τοῦτο ἐποίησάς μοι, ὅτι οὐκ ἀπήγγειλάς μοι ὅτι γυνή σού ἐστιν;
hint: Pharaoh asks why Abram did not tell him.

notes.text: Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[having called|having called, having summoned, having called to himself, having invited|καλέω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Φαραω]] [[name:Αβραμ]] [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] why this [[you made|you made, you did, you produced, you created|ποιέω]] to me, [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] not [[you brought tidings|you brought tidings, you reported, you announced, you carried a report, you related and narrated|ἀπαγγέλλω]] to me [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[woman|woman, mistress and lady, wife and spouse, mortal woman|γυνή]] of you is?

greek: ἵνα τί εἶπας ὅτι Ἀδελφή μού ἐστιν; καὶ ἔλαβον αὐτὴν ἐμαυτῷ εἰς γυναῖκα. καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ ἡ γυνή σου ἐναντίον σου· λαβὼν ἀπότρεχε.
hint: Take your wife and go.

notes.text: *Why*, as at 4:6: ἵνα with τί and the verb left out.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[that|that, in order that|ἵνα]] what [[you said|you said, you spoke, you declared, you called by name, you told|λέγω]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] sister of me is? and [[I took|I took, I received, I took hold of and grasped and seized|λαμβάνω]] her for myself [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[a woman|a woman, a mistress and lady, a wife and spouse, a mortal woman|γυνή]]. and [[now at this very time|now at this very time, now, of the present, the present time, just now and but now, as it is and as the case now stands, in this case|νῦν]] [[lo|lo, behold, see there|ἰδού]] [[the woman|the woman, the mistress and lady, the wife and spouse|γυνή]] of you [[in the presence of|in the presence of, before, opposite and face to face, against|ἐναντίον]] of you; [[having taken|having taken, having received, having taken hold of and grasped and seized|λαμβάνω]] [[run off|run off, run away, run hard|ἀποτρέχω]].

greek: καὶ ἐνετείλατο Φαραω ἀνδράσιν περὶ Αβραμ συμπροπέμψαι αὐτὸν καὶ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ πάντα, ὅσα ἦν αὐτῷ, καὶ Λωτ μετʼ αὐτοῦ.
hint: Pharaoh has men escort Abram away, with Lot.

notes.text: [[flag]] Not in the Hebrew here: the Greek brings Lot into the verse from 13:1.
συμπροπέμπω, *to join in escorting*, one sense, plain text.

reading: and [[enjoined|enjoined, commanded|ἐντέλλομαι]] [[name:Φαραω]] [[to men|to men, to men in the prime of life|ἀνήρ]] [[round about|round about, around, about and near, about and for and on account of, about and concerning, for very|περί + genitive]] [[name:Αβραμ]] to join in escorting him and [[the woman|the woman, the mistress and lady, the wife and spouse|γυνή]] of him and [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]], [[as great as|as great as, as much as, as far as, as long as, as many as|ὅσος]] was to him, and [[name:Λωτ]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] him.
